features.name: Dashboard authentication and write gates (FinancialData access layer)
features.description: HTTP Basic Auth for every dashboard route, implemented as a signed-session "financial data access" proof with configuration/connection generations, a protected query cache, a subscription authority and a change bridge; plus the router write gates (:api_write same-origin + X-Aiur-Request header, :require_writable) and the startup credential gate (refuse non-loopback bind without both credentials; loopback fails closed). Config: observability.dashboard_writable; env AIUR_DASHBOARD_USERNAME, AIUR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD.
features.usage_evidence: Every dashboard request passes through it. Credential names present in 5 dotenv files (2 private). observability.dashboard_writable set in 1 of 7 configs (private). Operational cost observed: boot.out.log in 5 retained runs warns "environment precedence conflict: AIUR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD is set to different values in ~/.aiur/.env and ./.env", and the Stream Deck sidecar journal shows 8,466 "Stream Deck token request failed (unauthorized)" retries (journalctl --user -u aiur-streamdeck.service).
features.rationale: Authentication is required, but 1,108 lines of generation proofs, per-connection cache scoping and a subscription authority guard one local single-operator dashboard whose only secret is a Basic-Auth pair. The complexity did not prevent the observed failure mode (mismatched passwords across dotenv files silently locking out the deck).
features.rewrite_notes: One Basic-Auth plug (constant-time compare) + one writable flag + the same-origin/X-Aiur-Request check for writes; drop FinancialData/FinancialDataAccess generations, proofs and SubscriptionAuthority. Keep the bind rule (non-loopback needs credentials). Resolve credentials from one source so the dashboard and the sidecar cannot disagree.

features.name: TUI agent-list board
features.description: The foreground terminal board (pane 0.0): one row per ticket with state glyphs, runtime, backend/model, progress bar, LATEST event, attention marker, warm-pane markers, max-agents chip, events ticker, help overlay; keys up/down/j/k, enter, shift+enter/O, space (pause/resume), left/right (concurrency cap), a (attach), r (remote control), v (layout), ? (help), q (quit).
entry_points: aiur --bg --interactive then bare aiur to attach
features.usage_evidence: No usage telemetry exists for key presses. Human (aiur transcript 2026-08-21): "what is the flag for me to run aiurdev and connect TUI to existing run"; 2026-09-09 asked to keep "chat via the TUI". Khala Executor drove the TUI via tmux (103 send-keys, 63 capture-pane Bash hits, 2026-09-24..26). Launch mix in Executor Bash commands: --bg 77 vs bare attach/foreground 18 (all repos). Retained run logs (~/.aiur/logs, 39 runs 2026-09-15..09-26): 30 have log/boot.out.log, which aiur-engine.sh:906 writes only in background mode; all runs with agent event logs are among them, so no working run in that window had the board. aiur-run skill: "Background mode is intentionally headless; observe it through the control commands, not TUI panes."
features.rationale: A real but secondary surface: agent Executors use `aiur agents`/`status`, and the human attaches sometimes. 4,240 lib lines render what `aiur agents` prints, with warmth markers that exist only to explain opencode slot pre-warm state (ui-23).
features.rewrite_notes: Rebuild as a thin renderer over the same agents read model the CLI uses (one row DTO); drop warm-slot markers, perf/warmth intakes and the debug events ticker. Keep keys enter/space/arrows/?/q. Note: no Executor transcript uses --bg --interactive (see ui-32).

features.name: tmux integration, isolated tmux config and Ctrl-key bridges
features.description: Aiur.Tmux command bus (per-socket, control-mode protocol parsing, mock transport), isolated tmux.conf (no prefix, extended keys, sync output, pane titles; ~/.config/aiur/tmux.conf override), Ctrl+C 3-state and Ctrl+Q hide bindings via scripts/aiur-pane-ctrlc -> POST /api/v1/pane/interrupt|hide, @aiur_control_url tmux option, launcher watchdog self-halt.
features.usage_evidence: Every run (including --bg) creates the tmux lifetime-holder session; live check: tmux -L aiur-<user>-<key> list-panes shows the current run session. Pane endpoints: 23 /api/v1/pane/hide and 10 /interrupt curl mentions across all transcripts (rg). The meta visual check reads @aiur_control_url from the tmux socket to find the dashboard.
features.rationale: Needed while the TUI and lifetime holder exist; two copies of aiur.tmux.conf (109 and 86 lines) and a control-mode parser are more than a pane splitter needs.
features.rewrite_notes: One tmux.conf; plain tmux commands instead of control-mode protocol parsing; keep the Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Q bridge.
features.docs: website/docs-app/guide/tui.md; AGENTS.md (driving the TUI from a non-TTY agent)

features.name: opencode chat-pane renderer (slots, attach pool, SQLite injection, chat-completions bridge)
features.description: Chat panes are opencode TUI instances: Aiur boots pre-warmed opencode-serve + opencode-attach slot panes in a hidden tmux window, injects every agent transcript (Claude/Codex) as rows into opencode's SQLite DB (~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db) and PATCHes parts so the attached TUI re-renders, streams live turns through an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions bridge with __aiur_turn__ markers, installs an aiur opencode theme, and GCs sessions. Config: pre_warmed_sessions, opencode.prewarm_disabled, opencode.db_path.
modules: src/lib/aiur/opencode/** (45 modules incl. slot*, attach_pool, session_writer, db, chat_completions/*, hidden_window, warmth_report, turn_markers, event_row)
entry_points: enter on a board row (opens a slot pane)
features.usage_evidence: Started only in non-headless runs (aiur.ex:478 "Chat-pane machinery - UI-only, never read by a headless run"); no working run in the retained 09-15..09-26 window was foreground (see ui-20). pre_warmed_sessions set in 7 of 7 configs (2 private; public values 3, 3, 0, 2) because `aiur init` scaffolds it; opencode.prewarm_disabled 0 of 7. Git: 48 commits to src/lib/aiur/opencode (10 fix-like subjects).
features.rationale: The single largest UI subsystem (9,050 lib + 5,210 test) exists to borrow opencode's renderer for agents that are not opencode, by writing into another tool's private SQLite schema (pinned row shapes, verified_min version) and faking chat-completion turns. It is idle in headless runs, which are the norm for agent Executors. Keep the capability (chat with an agent in the terminal), replace the mechanism.
features.rewrite_notes: Replace with a native chat pane: `aiur chat <ticket>` that tails the shared per-agent event feed (ui-06) and sends input through AgentChat, rendered with a small ANSI/markdown formatter (~500-800 lines). Or open the backend's own TUI (claude/codex resume) in the pane. Drop pre_warmed_sessions/opencode.* keys, slot pool, SQLite injection, theme install and warmth report.

features.name: Alert sounds
features.description: Plays a sound per alert topic: topic->sound YAML map (.aiur/alerts, scaffolded by `aiur init` from macOS/Linux templates) or built-in OS sounds by category, player probing afplay/paplay/canberra-gtk-play/aplay. Config: alerts.enabled (default true), alerts.use_os_default_sounds, alerts.sound_dir, alerts.alerts_file.
features.usage_evidence: alerts.* set in 5 of 7 configs (2 private, values not reported). The public ones: ~/.aiur/config and ~/.aiur/config.archon set alerts.enabled: false (with use_os_default_sounds: true), archon sets alerts.enabled: false. The aiur and kevinweaver-dev repo configs omit alerts, so the default mapping mode resolves bare names under ~/alerts, which does not exist on this host (ls ~/alerts: no such directory) -> silent. So no public configuration on this host can play a sound.
features.rationale: Disabled or silently inert everywhere it can be checked; ~700 lib lines plus a 245-line topic map to keep in sync with alert topics (the July inventory already found stale keys in it).
features.rewrite_notes: Delete sound playback and the four alerts.* keys; if an audible cue is wanted, expose one generic "on alert run command" hook (alerts stay in the alert feed). Keep alert message definitions with the alerts surface.

features.name: UI launch switches (foreground attach, --bg, --bg --interactive, --no-dashboard, --host, --debug)
features.description: How a run chooses its UI: bare `aiur` starts the foreground board or attaches to this checkout's session (engine injects --interactive); --bg is headless (no board, no chat panes, dashboard on); --bg --interactive keeps an attachable TUI; --no-dashboard suppresses the listener (refused when Remote Control is configured); --host overrides the bind host; --debug enables verbose logging.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh (owned by the CLI surface; not counted here)
features.usage_evidence: Transcript scan (features/scratch-ui/scan_transcripts.py) of Executor transcripts five public transcript segments (571/150/262/87/0 files) and one private source (111 files; no private path retained), counting only Bash tool_use commands and user-typed text; hits dated 2026-09-26 include today's research sessions. Bash hits: --bg 77 (aiur 53, architecture-docs 18, archon 4, khala 2); bare aiur/aiurdev 18; --debug 50; --host 27; --no-dashboard 3; "--bg --interactive" 0. Retained runs: 30 of 39 background.
features.rationale: --bg (headless) is the dominant mode; --bg --interactive has no recorded use and adds a third TUI lifecycle to the engine and aiur.ex supervision tree.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep two modes: headless daemon, and a separate `aiur tui` client that attaches to any running daemon (removes the need for --interactive and the foreground special case).
